name: Malcolm Lund
life: “I still remember cutting replacement glass for an irreplaceable frame.” On Thursday, near Paper & Pine Books, Malcolm starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I want to make her a new mirror in the same shape. She explained that shape was the least important part.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a black overshirt with pearl buttons and a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining. Malcolm has a small notch in the left eyebrow, with a smooth side part with one rebellious curl. Malcolm starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak during a conversation.
personality: Malcolm listens for the familiar version of a story and then for the one detail that changes it. Friends bring problems here when they want to be heard twice.
agenda: To offer a new mirror without promising the same history.
family: Bianca Spencer is Malcolm’s second cousin. Malcolm is free to hang up first. Bianca makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The late crossing*, Bianca says, “I can pay toward fuel but can't say it in front of my kids.”
connections: Seth Massey. A sample of new glass offers a familiar apartment reflection without pretending to be the original mirror.
